subject: HelixOps VPC: intermittent inference queue saturation causing 503s — immediate tuning and exec visibility
messages:
From: Marco Rossi <marco@helixops.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Gupta <elena@helixops.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden p95 spike + 503s in our private VPC cluster (urgent)

Kimberly / Redwood team,

We started seeing intermittent 503s and a steep p95 jump on our private inference cluster around 07:55 PST. Throughput dropped ~40% on our critical route (recommendation/recall model) and tail latencies spiked. I've attached a quick KPI snapshot from our monitoring.

Key items:
- Time window: 07:55–08:05 PST (spikes repeat intermittently)
- Error surface: 503s concentrated on shard-7 and shard-12
- Business impact: user-facing failures for ~2k DAUs; revenue hit noticeable on the aam endpoint

We need an urgent runbook: recommended mitigations (cache warming, routing fallback, capacity burst) and a clear timeline. We're also prepared to grant temporary permission for you to scale burst capacity in our VPC if that will help. Please escalate to whoever handles private deployments — exec visibility recommended if this becomes prolonged.

Attachments: kpi_snapshot_20280110.csv

Thanks,
Marco Rossi
CTO, HelixOps
marco@helixops.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Rossi <marco@helixops.com>
Cc: Elena Gupta <elena@helixops.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-10T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike + 503s in our private VPC cluster (urgent)

Marco / Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the KPI file. We're on it.

Immediate ask: please confirm we have permission to temporarily increase HelixOps' dedicated burst pool by one additional GPU instance and to enable routing to the quantized model variant for the next 90 minutes. Both mitigations should reduce immediate 503s while we diagnose.

What we'll do now (short-term):
- Trigger burst capacity (if you approve) and monitor 1-minute p95 and 503 rate. (owner: Laura)
- Warm KV cache for hot prefixes on affected shards (owner: Connor)
- Collect core inference logs from shard-7 and shard-12 and upload to your shared location (owner: Vivek)
- Open ticket SUP-4129 and start a live runbook thread with timestamps and actions.

Please confirm permission now so we can act. If you prefer an on-call phone bridge, we can open one immediately.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) Trigger +1 burst GPU in HelixOps dedicated pool and enable fallback to quantized variant for aam endpoint (Laura)
2) Warm hot prefixes and pre-populate KV cache for shard-7 and shard-12 (Connor)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-10T11:50:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixOps VPC — immediate action plan and owners (SUP-4129)

Quick status and findings from initial triage: uploaded core logs (svc_core_logs_01010.tar.gz) to their bucket. Observations:
- High KV cache cold-miss rate on shard-7 and shard-12 during the window; miss rate correlates with the 503 spikes.
- Two hot routes (aam-recs-v2 and user-sig-scorer) are creating bursty KV usage on a subset of replicas due to uneven sharding.
- We see frequent small batches ~1–2 tokens causing high per-token overhead.

Short-term mitigations applied (11:35 PST):
- Enabled routing fallback to quantized aam-recs-v2 (reduced memory pressure).
- Warmed top 200 prefixes for affected shards.
- Temporarily increased max_batch_size from 8 to 16 for the aegis-serving group in their config; monitor for p95 impact.

Recommended next steps (medium-term):
- Run a targeted kernel recompile for the custom attention path on the affected instance family (owner: infra optimization team) — will improve throughput under higher batch sizes.
- Rebalance hot routes across replicas to avoid shard hot spots.
- Add KV cache prefetch for top routes as a persistent optimization.

Caveat: increasing batch size can lower cost but may bump p50; we prioritized reducing 503s for customer SLA.

I'll keep posting progress into SUP-4129.

— Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Rossi <marco@helixops.com>, Elena Gupta <elena@helixops.com>

Date: 2028-01-12T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: HelixOps incident update: stabilization achieved — follow-up runbook and next steps

Marco / Elena — closing the loop on the immediate escalation. Summary:
- Mitigations applied 2028-01-10 starting at 11:35 PST (routing fallback, cache warm, +1 burst GPU, batch-size increase).
- Observed outcome: 503 rate fell from peak ~4.6% to <0.2% within 18 minutes of mitigations; p95 for the aam endpoint improved from ~1.9s to ~450ms under typical load.
- We have uploaded the investigation artifacts and the short playbook to your emergency bucket.

Attachments: playbook_v1.pdf (short-term runbook + rollback), kpi_snapshot_20280110.csv, svc_core_logs_01010.tar.gz

Planned follow-ups (scheduled):
1) Kernel recompile and benchmark on the affected instance family — target window 2028-01-18 (owner: infra optimization)
2) Permanent rebalance of hot routes during the next maintenance window (owner: platform ops)
3) Post-mortem and runbook refinement; we'll share a 1-page exec brief by 2028-01-15.

We understand the business impact and will continue to prioritize HelixOps' private deployment tuning. If you'd like an executive-level note, I can loop in Laura for a 15-minute briefing.

Kimberly Park
